question: The electrostatic potential $V(x)$ along the axis of a short electric dipole is measured and plotted against the distance $x$ from its center. The graph shows that at $x = 2\text{m}$, the potential $V = 0.5\text{V}$. This dipole is now placed in a uniform external electric field $E = 1.0 \times 10^5$ N/C. What is the maximum possible potential energy ($U_{max}$) of the dipole in this field, and what is the work done by the electric field ($W_{field}$) in rotating the dipole from its stable to unstable equilibrium position?
